title: Core ideas in biology
description: How life works, from cells and DNA to evolution and the flow of energy.

ideas.title: Cells
ideas.summary: Every living thing is made of cells, and every cell comes from an earlier cell.

items.q: What is the main difference between a prokaryotic cell and a eukaryotic cell?
items.a: A eukaryotic cell has a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; a prokaryotic cell has neither

items.q: During aerobic respiration in a typical animal cell, which organelle produces most of the ATP?
Which structure in a cell builds proteins?
What is a cell's outer membrane mainly made of?
items.a: A phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it

ideas.title: DNA and the genetic code
ideas.summary: DNA stores instructions in a four-letter code, which cells copy into RNA and then read out as protein.

items.q: In DNA, which base pairs with adenine?
What does the central dogma of molecular biology describe?
items.a: Sequence information can pass from nucleic acids to protein, but not from protein back to nucleic acids or other proteins

items.q: What is the process called in which a cell copies a gene's DNA into messenger RNA?
In the genetic code, how many bases make up one codon, the unit that specifies an amino acid?
Which two scientists proposed the double helix structure of DNA in 1953?
items.a: James Watson and Francis Crick, drawing on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray images

ideas.title: Inheritance
ideas.summary: Genes come in pairs, one copy from each parent, and are dealt out afresh to each new generation.

items.q: Which friar's experiments with pea plants, published in 1866, founded the science of genetics?
How many chromosomes does a typical human body cell contain?
In genetics, what is an allele?
items.a: One of the alternative versions of a gene

items.q: Which type of cell division halves the number of chromosomes to make eggs and sperm?

ideas.title: Evolution by natural selection
ideas.summary: When heritable traits affect survival and reproduction, populations change over the generations.

items.q: Who wrote On the Origin of Species, and in what year was it published?
Which naturalist arrived at the idea of natural selection independently of Charles Darwin?
In biology, what is natural selection?
items.a: Heritable traits that help survival and reproduction become more common over generations

items.q: In evolution, what is the ultimate source of new genetic variation?

ideas.title: Energy in living things
ideas.summary: Photosynthesis stores the energy of sunlight in sugar, and respiration releases it for cells to use as ATP.

items.q: What does photosynthesis take in, and what does it produce?
items.a: It takes in carbon dioxide, water and light, and produces glucose and oxygen

items.q: Which molecule is the main energy currency of the cell?
In which organelle of a plant cell does photosynthesis take place?
What does aerobic cellular respiration do?
items.a: It breaks down glucose with oxygen to make ATP, giving off carbon dioxide and water

ideas.title: Ecosystems
ideas.summary: Energy flows one way through a food chain and is mostly lost at each step, while matter is recycled.

items.q: In an ecosystem, what are organisms called that make their own food from sunlight or chemicals?
In a food chain, roughly what share of the energy at one trophic level passes on to the next?
In ecology, what is the carrying capacity of an environment?
items.a: The largest population of a species that it can support over the long term
